summary: Records errors found in the Megaco/H.248 protocol document, with changes proposed to resolve them. It is historic and was replaced by RFC 3015.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a list of typos and mistakes in an early rule book, with the fixes. A newer rule book replaced it.

questions: what errors were in the megaco protocol
subtitle: Corrections and clarifications to the Megaco protocol specification.

tldr.problem: RFC 2885 defined Megaco, a protocol for controlling media gateways and handling multimedia calls. After publication, implementers found ambiguities, contradictions, and editorial errors that needed clarification.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC documents the errors found in RFC 2885 and proposes fixes for each one, ranging from missing references and undefined behavior to syntax errors and incorrect section statements.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2886 was obsoleted by RFC 3015, which incorporated the errata directly into a consolidated specification.

today: RFC 2886 is Historic and was obsoleted by RFC 3015 in November 2000. RFC 3015 incorporates the errata from RFC 2886 directly into a consolidated specification of the Megaco Protocol Version 1.0.

sections.title: What Megaco Is and Why It Needed Corrections
sections.content:
Megaco (defined in RFC 2885) is a protocol for controlling media gateways and coordinating multimedia communications. It describes how a Media Gateway Controller (MGC) manages Media Gateways (MGs) and how terminations (logical connections to endpoints) are configured and used.

After RFC 2885 was published, readers and implementers found errors: missing references, unclear procedures, contradictions between sections, and syntax ambiguities in the ASN.1 and ABNF formats. This RFC collects those errors and specifies the intended corrections.
sections.plainLanguage: Megaco is a set of rules for controlling telephone switches. This RFC lists the parts of the rule book that were unclear or wrong, and explains the fixes.

sections.title: Categories of Errors Found
sections.content:
The errata in RFC 2885 fell into several categories. Editorial errors include missing or unused references, missing acronym definitions, and incorrect section titles. For example, an unused reference to Q.724 should be deleted, and explanations for GSM and IVR were missing from the abbreviations section.

Technical errors were more serious: ambiguities in how descriptors should be processed (the order was fixed in ASN.1 but variable in ABNF), unclear behavior for empty descriptors, and contradictions about which properties are retained when a termination returns to the null context.

Syntax errors affected both the formal notation and the way certain fields could be specified. For instance, the DigitMap descriptor initially made the value field mandatory when it should have been optional, and the EventBufferDescriptor was incorrectly defined.
sections.plainLanguage: The errors were of three kinds: typos and missing labels, confusing or contradictory rules, and syntax mistakes in the formal definitions.

sections.title: Key Corrections in Descriptors and Procedures
sections.content:
Several important errata clarified how service functions should process packet metadata. The TerminationID section was unclear about how wildcard union responses should look; the errata added an example showing that properties are merged when matching multiple terminations.

The Events Descriptor section had multiple problems. It was unclear whether events trigger side effects at detection time, processing time, or notification time. The errata clarified that recognition of an event causes active signals to stop (unless KeepActive is set). Procedural steps for handling events and digit maps were rewritten to avoid infinite loops and to properly define when unmatched events are recognized.

The Signals Descriptor needed better definition of the notifyCompletion parameter, which tells the controller which signal-completion outcomes to report. The errata expanded it from a simple flag to a bit string with four cases: timeout, interrupt, replacement, or other reasons.
sections.plainLanguage: The main fixes clarified how devices respond to events, when signals should stop playing, and how to report when a signal finishes.

sections.title: Fixes to Audit Commands and Message Transport
sections.content:
The AuditValue command had several issues. It was unclear how to retrieve multiple items of the same descriptor type (such as multiple digit maps), and the behavior of wildcarded context IDs (like ALL, which does not include the null context) was ambiguous. The errata clarified that multiple instances may be returned and that ALL excludes the null context.

Transport over UDP needed clarification. The interim Authentication Header (AH) scheme could be shorter than initially stated (24 hex digits instead of 32), and the errata clarified which UDP port should be used. Transaction-level procedures were also tightened: transaction ID 0 was reserved for reporting syntax errors when no other ID is available, and exponential backoff was made mandatory for retransmission timers to prevent congestion.
sections.plainLanguage: The fixes explained how to ask for multiple things at once, clarified the UDP details, and made retransmission behavior more consistent.

sections.title: Corrections to ASN.1 and ABNF Syntax Definitions
sections.content:
The formal syntax had numerous issues. The ASN.1 used reserved values for the NULL context, wildcard CHOOSE, and wildcard ALL, but these needed to be reserved in the text-encoded ABNF syntax as well. The EventBufferDescriptor was incorrectly portrayed as a sequence of ObservedEvent when it should be a sequence of EventSpec.

The DigitMap syntax was clarified to allow unnamed digit maps to be returned in audit responses. The PropertyParm type needed a new choice to support sub-lists (parameters with multiple values at once). Capitalization inconsistencies and missing extensions (indicated by ellipses in ASN.1) were fixed.

The ABNF alternativeValue production was rewritten to remove ambiguity between sub-lists, sets of alternatives, and ranges, each now having distinct syntax.
sections.plainLanguage: Technical fixes to the formal grammar made sure that all parts of the rules were consistent and unambiguous.
